methodology.playerValueCurve: v(adp) = 100 * exp(-0.028 * (adp - 1)); floor 1.0 when ADP unknown

constructionNotes: thin starting slot: TE (Sam LaPorta, ADP 124.6)
teams.verdict: The cleanest board in the league: first in value captured, first in starting lineup, first in ceiling, first in bench. Stafford at 168 against a market price of 75 was the draft's best pure value; LaPorta four rounds early was the only real leak. When one team leads all four weighted categories, the letter writes itself.

picks.comment: The consensus 1.01, and he made it.
Four rounds ahead of price. The one pick in this draft the model would appeal.
Priced at 75, drafted at 168. The best value in the entire draft.

teams.verdict: A perfect construction score and no panicked picks. Henry at 18 against a price of 10 and Burrow at 7.07 anchored a draft that paid a small premium at tight end and let value come to it everywhere else. Docked to A- for the thin backfield behind Henry and the Allgeier reach. Otherwise this was textbook.

picks.comment: Priced at 10. The room let a top-ten pick fall to 18.
A 12-pick premium for the tight end edge. Defensible.
49 picks past price. Half of the best late-receiver haul in the draft.

teams.verdict: Best backfield drafted, a real WR1, and a perfect construction score. The B+ instead of higher comes from a receiver room that thins out immediately after Nico Collins and a Rachaad White pick 26 ahead of price. Maye at 6.09 was strong quarterback timing. This roster is one trade from an A, and its manager said as much in the chat.

picks.comment: The quarterback timing everyone else wished they'd had.
Priced at 119. Twenty-six picks early for a backup.
37 picks past price, and immediately his WR3. That is the compliment and the problem.

teams.verdict: Second-best value capture in the draft: Meyers, McMillan, and a 132nd-pick defense all came well past price. The ceiling on the grade is what the value bought. The starting lineup scored ninth, with quarterback addressed at pick 118 and tight end acquired at a discount for a reason. Excellent shopping, modest pantry.

picks.comment: 36 picks ahead of market. The one true reach.
30 past price. Good value at the position he waited too long on.
55 picks past price in the final round.

teams.verdict: A top-heavy grade: Bijan and Pickens carried the ceiling score, and rounds 10 through 16 (Addison, Shakir, Nailor) rescued the value column. Between those bookends sat the shakiest RB middle in the draft, with Price 26 early and Kamara 36 early. Perfect construction, wobbly contents.

picks.comment: 26 picks ahead of price for the RB2 job this roster badly needed.
Priced at 158. A bet against the market's obituary.
43 past price in round 16. Free money.

teams.verdict: A market-clean draft with one big positional imbalance. Brown, Egbuka, and Daniels all came at or past price; Warren at 5.09 was the lone real reach. Seven receivers against three startable running backs cost construction points, and the ceiling rests on rookie receivers hitting. Balanced scores, no standout column, a straight B.

picks.comment: 1.09 against a market price of 14.8. Aggressive, and the market shrugged.
15 picks ahead of price. The reach.
15 past price. Possibly the pick that ages best.
The RB depth plan, in its entirety.

teams.verdict: Elite starters at receiver and quarterback set against the weakest drafted starting backfield in the league. Goff at 188 against a price of 100 was the draft's second-best value. The B- is the average of an A top and a D backfield; no grading system splits that difference cleanly.

picks.comment: Asim's own review, in the chat, was that this pick might have "jacked up my roster." The model says it was market price.
88 past price. The best insurance pick of the draft.

teams.verdict: Remove one pick and this is a B+. Lloyd at 67 against a price of 157 was the draft's largest reach and sank the value column by itself. Hurts, Jeudy, and Ridley were quality timing. Graded exactly as drafted: eleven sound rounds and one that will be cited in this space all season.

picks.comment: Priced at 157. The largest reach in the draft by a factor of two.
A top-five quarterback at a discount.
47 past price. The final rounds nearly balanced the Lloyd books. Nearly.

constructionNotes: thin starting slot: TE (Juwan Johnson, ADP 160.8)
teams.verdict: The first five rounds graded among the best in the league; the last eleven among the worst. Rodriguez (41 early) and Coleman (39 early) drained the value score, and a second quarterback in round 9 spent a pick the roster didn't owe. Cook insurance via Ray Davis was smart. C+ is the exact midpoint of two different drafts.

picks.comment: "He fell." He was priced at 55.9 and taken at 56. He arrived on schedule.
A second quarterback, taken directly in front of the one manager who needed one.
His own James Cook insurance. "I got my own cuffs."

teams.verdict: Last in value captured. Jeanty, Washington (47 early), Keaton Mitchell (36 early), and Butker (35 early) all came at real premiums, while quarterback waited until pick 155. Lawrence at that price was excellent in isolation, but value on your own QB1 in round 13 is a symptom, not a plan. The young receiver core keeps this at C+.

picks.comment: 47 picks ahead of price. The sickness, documented.
65 past price. Great pick, alarming plan: this is the QB1.
The all-Jets endgame begins.

teams.verdict: The construction score, lowest in the league, tells the story: a kicker at pick 106, a defense at 111, and seven running backs without a locked starting job among them. St. Brown, Jefferson, and McBride was as good an opening three as anyone's. Eleventh in value, last in bench. The C averages a superstar draft with an org-chart problem.

picks.comment: With St. Brown already rostered: the league's best receiver duo, assembled by pick 15.
34 picks ahead of price, on the stated hope that "it's time."
A kicker at pick 106, priced at 134. The construction score never recovered.

constructionNotes: thin starting slot: TE (Travis Kelce, ADP 119.9)
teams.verdict: Frozen in time, as promised: last in starting lineup, last in ceiling. Hampton 11 early and Likely 51 early were premiums paid at exactly the wrong spots, while Kelce at 180 and Godwin at 108 rescued the value column to mid-pack. The bench score is real consolation. The C- grades the lineup he has to start, not the one the chat believes in.

picks.comment: 11 picks ahead of price at 1.12. The market wanted him at the two-three turn.
51 ahead of price, at a position later solved for free.
60 past price, while the chat spent ten minutes pricing in his wedding.
